content: Tinea, also known as dermatophytosis, refers to a group of fungal infections of the skin caused by parasitic fungi known as dermatophytes. When these infections occur on the body, they often present as characteristic enlarging, raised, red rings, commonly referred to as ringworm. If the infection affects the skin of the feet, it manifests as athlete's foot, while involvement in the groin area is termed jock itch. When the nails are affected, the condition is called onychomycosis. In such cases, the nails may become thickened, discolored, and eventually crumble and detach from the nail bed. These infections are prevalent among adults, with approximately 20% of the population experiencing one of these conditions at any given time. Symptoms often worsen during the summer months and tend to improve during the winter. Various species of fungi are responsible for these infections, with dermatophytes from the genera Trichophyton and Microsporum being the most common causative agents.
